explanation: Cheek kissing is not a standard greeting in Singapore; a handshake is the default across all communities, and some Malay or Indian Singaporeans may prefer not to shake hands with the opposite gender at all for religious or cultural reasons. Cheek kissing does happen among close friends in more Westernized or expatriate circles, but it isn't the norm for a first meeting.
local_tip: Default to a light handshake; if someone of the opposite gender doesn't extend their hand, follow their lead and offer a nod or a hand over your heart instead.
regional_note: Malay and Indian Singaporeans may avoid cross-gender handshakes for religious reasons; Chinese Singaporeans may add a slight nod to a handshake. None of these groups treat cheek kissing as a standard greeting.

also_check.note: Cheek kissing (la bise) is a standard greeting among friends and acquaintances, with the number of kisses varying by region.
Physical greetings are minimal; a bow is standard and cheek kissing would be seen as unusually intimate.
Cheek kissing is a common greeting, even between new acquaintances.
